source.title: NeuronMotif: Deciphering cis-regulatory codes by layer-wise demixing of deep neural networks
source.authors: Zheng Wei; Kui Hua; Lei Wei; Shining Ma; Rui Jiang; Xuegong Zhang; Yanda Li; Wing Hong Wong; Xiao-Wo Wang

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. The document has a bioRxiv preprint header, while the supplied metadata identifies the PNAS publication.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures mixtures of motifs represented by convolutional neurons and reports how those mixtures vary with layer and architecture. This bears conceptually on whether a neuron can represent multiple features for reasons other than capacity pressure, but it does not test superposition geometry or feature sparsity.
record.gate_note: Results about motif discovery accuracy, model prediction performance, dead neurons, ATAC-seq footprints, and comparisons with interpretation methods are not recorded as rows because they do not measure the polysemantic motif mixtures relevant to V3. Values in figures are not transcribed unless the text explicitly describes the result.
record.test_reason: This is a genomics CNN interpretation paper from 2021 that predates the superposition paper and never mentions superposition, capacity or sparsity. It decomposes convolutional neurons' preferred sequences into shifted motifs (an artefact of max-pooling invariance) and 'synonymous' motifs. It diagnoses synonymous mixing only indirectly: it compares the consensus-sequence activation with the maximum activation of sampled sequences. This is a related construct, not a rate of polysemanticity. The study never manipulates or measures capacity pressure, so it cannot show polysemanticity arising without it, as V3 states. The architecture changes (BD-10, DD-10) alter depth, kernel size, pooling and kernel count all at once. The findings are recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a test of V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors conclude that convolutional neurons mix shifted motifs (from max-pooling) and synonymous motifs. NeuronMotif decouples these mixtures and recovers motif grammars supported by JASPAR, the literature and ATAC-seq footprints. They treat synonymous mixtures as noise that makes neurons sensitive to adversarial changes, and say architectures with larger kernels and pooling are more prone to it. Deeper small-kernel models (BD-10, DD-10) suppress the mixing and predict better.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a genetic-algorithm-based sequence sampler and layer-wise K-means demixing of motifs in biological convolutional networks; it does not use the toy-model method or geometry measurements from the superposition source.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported mixture problem varies with layer and model architecture; the text also attributes suppression to strong regularization in DeepSEA and to the deeper, smaller-kernel architectures BD-10 and DD-10.

fits_no_version.finding: In DNA-sequence CNNs, single neurons respond to several 'synonymous' motifs. The text gives reverse complements as one case and reports this mixing as common in Basset L3 but not L2. The authors tie it to weak coupling from large kernels and pooling, and report it suppressed in deeper, small-kernel models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture choices (kernel size, pooling, regularization) affect how often convolutional neurons mix distinct input patterns, separately from width or capacity.

fits_no_version.finding: A derivation, for a linear first-layer unit, shows that mixing two dissimilar synonymous motifs forces the weight norm toward zero and lowers the maximum activation. The authors therefore treat such mixtures as noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Units that mix dissimilar inputs have smaller weights and lower peak activation, which is a cost of polysemantic mixing.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America (metadata); the supplied paper text carries a bioRxiv preprint header.
record.problems: The motif-mixture findings are mostly qualitative in the supplied text, with no numerical mixture rates or uncertainty estimates. The results concern biological sequence CNNs and do not directly measure capacity pressure, sparsity, or superposition geometry.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows meeting the claim-version criteria were identified.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweeps or feature geometry.
No capacity manipulation, and no test of feature importance against dedicated or shared dimensions.
Polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure is not tested: there is no capacity contrast and no comparison with superposition.

missing.what: A theoretical derivation (Methods) that synonymous-motif mixing implies |k|→0 and a lower maximum activation. It bears conceptually on the costs of polysemantic mixing but is not tied to any version.
missing.locator: Methods, 'The side-effect for the ANs representing different synonymous motifs'

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' for V3 is overstated. The paper's 'mixture' concept mostly concerns position invariance and reverse-complement equivalence, not distinct features sharing a neuron. It neither engages with nor controls for capacity. All results are qualitative readings of scatter plots (Fig. 4b,c) with no rates.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, feature-direction geometry, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometry are tested.
No capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, or relationship between feature importance and sharing is tested.
The study does not compare its motif-mixture mechanism with superposition or establish that it occurs without capacity pressure in language models.
No LLM representations or SAE feature recovery are studied.
No SAE dictionary features or claims of canonical, complete, stable units are studied.
The study does not test whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Basset
rows.operation_detail: Compared motif consensus-sequence activation with the maximum activation of sampled sequences to diagnose synonymous-motif mixtures.
rows.measure: Agreement between activation of motif consensus sequences and maximum activation of sampled sequences
rows.value: The two indicators are described as almost consistent.
rows.locator: Results, “DCNN diagnosis and architecture design guidance”; Fig. 4c
rows.note: The authors describe little discrepancy for L2, unlike the reported L3 result.
rows.check: The consensus-versus-max-activation agreement is an indirect, qualitative diagnostic of synonymous-motif mixing. It is not a polysemanticity measure and has no capacity contrast, so it cannot show V3's effect. No numbers are given; the text says the indicators are 'almost consistent'.

rows.subject: Basset
rows.operation_detail: Compared motif consensus-sequence activation with the maximum activation of sampled sequences to diagnose synonymous-motif mixtures.
rows.measure: Discrepancy between motif consensus-sequence activation and maximum activation of sampled sequences
rows.value: Many decoupled motifs have negative consensus-sequence activations that are described as severely deviating from the maximum activation; the authors attribute most problematic motifs to mixtures of different synonymous motifs.
rows.locator: Results, “DCNN diagnosis and architecture design guidance”; Fig. 4c
rows.note: The reported measurement is a motif-mixture diagnostic in a DNA-sequence CNN, not a test of superposition.
rows.check: The diagnostic shows mixing in Basset L3, but it is not attributed to, or contrasted with, capacity pressure. The mechanism the authors propose is weak coupling from large kernels and pooling. The result is qualitative only.

rows.subject: DeepSEA
rows.operation_detail: Diagnosed synonymous-motif noise using motif activation indicators.

conditions.value: original DeepSEA architecture with strong regularization

rows.value: Strong regularization is described as successfully suppressing learning these noises, at the cost of producing dead neurons.
rows.locator: Results, “DCNN diagnosis and architecture design guidance”; Fig. 4b
rows.note: The text does not provide a numeric mixture rate.
rows.check: This is a qualitative statement that strong regularization suppresses synonymous-motif noise at the cost of dead neurons. There is no unregularized DeepSEA control and no capacity measure.

rows.subject: BD-10
rows.operation_detail: Diagnosed synonymous-motif mixtures using motif activation indicators.

conditions.value: 10 convolutional layers with small kernels and pooling structures

rows.value: The synonymous-motif problem is described as significantly suppressed; few dead kernels were found.
rows.locator: Results, “DCNN diagnosis and architecture design guidance”; Fig. 4c
rows.note: The text says the problem was suppressed, not that all mixtures were eliminated.
rows.check: This compares the authors' own redesigned architecture with Basset. Depth, kernel size, pooling and kernel count all change together, so the change in mixing cannot be tied to capacity or to any other single cause. The result is qualitative ('significant suppressed').

rows.subject: DD-10
rows.operation_detail: Diagnosed synonymous-motif mixtures using motif activation indicators.

conditions.value: 10 convolutional layers with small kernels and pooling structures

rows.value: The synonymous-motif problem is described as significantly suppressed; few dead kernels were found.
rows.locator: Results, “DCNN diagnosis and architecture design guidance”; Fig. 4b
rows.note: The text says the problem was suppressed, not that all mixtures were eliminated.
rows.check: This has the same problem as r4, for DD-10 compared with DeepSEA.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The study reports mixed synonymous motifs and discrepant motif consensus activations in this layer, consistent with multiple motif patterns being represented by neurons for a mechanism it associates with the network structure (r2).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Basset L2, regularized DeepSEA, BD-10, and DD-10
reader_labels.reason: The reported mixture diagnostic is nearly consistent in Basset L2, noise is described as suppressed in regularized DeepSEA, and the problem is significantly suppressed in BD-10 and DD-10 (r1, r3, r4, r5).
